newsitem.title: USA: Tribune says report shows circulation drop.
newsitem.headline: Tribune says report shows circulation drop.

text.p: Tribune Co said the most recent report from the Audit Bureau of Circulations for the six months ended September 30 showed a decline in average daily circulation for the Chicago Tribune by 0.6 percent, or 3,831 copies to 680,535 compared to a year ago.
It said the for same period, competitor Chicago Sun-Times, a Hollinger International Inc unit, saw average daily circulation gain by 1.6 percent or 7,625 copies to 496,030.
Tribune said its average Saturday circulation decreased 0.1 percent or by 580 copies to 609,151 and average Sunday circulation dropped 3.4 percent or by 37,186 to 1,046,777.
It said Sun-Times average Saturday circulation declined 0.7 percent or by 2,364 copies to 345,033 and average Sunday circulation fell 4.3 percent or by 19,898 to 442,905.
"Our Sunday circulation loss still reflects our newsstand price increase to $1.75 a year ago," said David Murphy, vice president and director of consumer marketing and sales for the Chicago Tribune.
Gruntal & Co Inc analyst Rita Zanella said "Tribune's 0.6 percent dip in average daily circulation is nothing to get alarmed about. We've factored in such declines."
Zanella called the 1.6 percent gain at the Chicago Sun-Times a positive for the company. "It bucks the trend," she told Reuters.
